core_obligations: Rewrite m_B/m_B^2 as H_1 of the naive cotangent complex of K over B and reduce to injectivity of H_1(NL_{K/A}) into m_B/m_B^2 (proof lines 10029-10031).
Compute the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for A to k to K to describe H_1(NL_{K/A}) (proof lines 10032-10041).
Produce the short exact sequence of cotangent spaces using that the special fibre is regular, together with flatness of A to B (proof lines 10042-10057).
Build the commutative diagram comparing the two sequences and identify its left vertical arrow as injective (proof lines 10058-10076).
Apply the snake lemma to conclude injectivity in the middle of the top row (proof lines 10077-10078).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a single injectivity statement (proof lines 10029-10041).
Build the two short exact sequences via regularity of the special fibre (proof lines 10042-10057).
Compare them functorially and check the left arrow (proof lines 10058-10076).
Finish with the snake lemma (proof lines 10077-10078).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies the beginning of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence for a formally smooth local homomorphism of Noetherian local rings at the residue field of the target: it shows that the connecting term H_1 of the naive cotangent complex injects into the cotangent space, so the sequence starts with a zero on the left. The proof reduces to that injectivity by quoting the exactness of the Jacobi-Zariski sequence and the identification of the cotangent space with H_1 of the relative naive cotangent complex, then rewrites the domain of the arrow through the sequence of the residue field extension, produces a short exact sequence for the cotangent spaces via the conormal sequence of a regular quotient, compares the two rows in a commutative diagram, and finishes by the snake lemma once injectivity of the left vertical arrow is known from the regular-fibre theorem. The argument is short but uses four external ingredients, each quoted exactly.
